properties.name: Missing Signer Check
properties.invariant_template: Every privileged instruction MUST validate that the expected signer account has actually signed the transaction.
properties.description: An instruction handler fails to verify that a required account has signed the transaction, allowing any user to invoke privileged operations (e.g. admin withdrawals, parameter changes) without authorization.
properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Signer<'info>` type or `#[account(signer)]` constraint for every authority account.

properties.name: Account Ownership Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every deserialized account MUST be validated to be owned by the expected program before use.
properties.description: An instruction accepts an account without verifying its owner program, allowing an attacker to pass a fake account owned by a different program with crafted data.

annotations.common_vuln: Using unchecked `AccountInfo` instead of typed `Account<'info, T>`

properties.remediation: Use Anchor typed accounts (`Account<'info, T>`) which automatically validate ownership and deserialization.

properties.name: PDA & Bump Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every PDA account MUST be derived with the correct seeds and its bump seed MUST be validated (stored or canonical).
properties.description: A Program Derived Address is accepted without verifying its derivation seeds or bump, allowing an attacker to supply a different PDA or a non-canonical bump to access/modify unintended state.
properties.remediation: Always use `#[account(seeds = [..], bump)]` constraints and store the canonical bump on initialization.

properties.name: Duplicate Account Aliasing
properties.invariant_template: When an instruction takes multiple accounts of the same type, each account MUST be proven distinct (no aliasing).
properties.description: An instruction handler accepts two accounts (e.g. `from` and `to`) without checking they are distinct. An attacker passes the same account for both, potentially doubling balances or bypassing transfer checks.

annotations.common_vuln: No key equality check between same-type accounts

properties.remediation: Add explicit `constraint = a.key() != b.key()` for every pair of same-type accounts.

properties.name: CPI Program-ID Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every Cross-Program Invocation MUST validate the target program's ID before invoking it.
properties.description: A CPI call is made using a program account passed by the user without verifying its program ID, allowing an attacker to redirect the CPI to a malicious program.

annotations.common_vuln: Using unchecked AccountInfo for CPI target program

properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Program<'info, T>` type for CPI target programs, or explicitly check `program.key() == expected_program_id`.

properties.name: Sysvar Account Validation
properties.invariant_template: Sysvar accounts (Clock, Rent, etc.) MUST be validated against their known addresses or accessed via sysvar API.
properties.description: A sysvar account (Rent, Clock, etc.) is accepted as a user-supplied AccountInfo without verifying it matches the canonical sysvar address, allowing data spoofing.
properties.remediation: Use Anchor's `Sysvar<'info, T>` type or `Clock::get()` / `Rent::get()` sysvar API.

properties.name: Arithmetic Overflow
properties.invariant_template: All arithmetic operations on token amounts and balances MUST use checked/saturating math to prevent overflow/underflow.
properties.description: Arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication) on u64 balances or amounts are performed without overflow checks, potentially wrapping around and creating or destroying value.
properties.remediation: Replace all `+`, `-`, `*` on financial values with `checked_add()`, `checked_sub()`, `checked_mul()` and handle the `None` case with a custom error.

properties.name: Signer & Authority Mismatch
properties.invariant_template: The signer of a privileged instruction MUST match the authority stored in the target account's state.
properties.description: An instruction checks that *some* account signed the transaction but does not verify that the signer matches the authority/owner stored in the account being modified.

annotations.common_vuln: Signer present but not matched against stored authority pubkey

properties.remediation: Use `#[account(has_one = authority)]` or explicitly compare `signer.key() == account.authority`.

properties.name: State Transition Invariant
properties.invariant_template: Account state transitions MUST follow a valid finite-state machine — illegal transitions MUST be rejected.
properties.description: An instruction modifies account state without validating the current state, allowing invalid transitions (e.g. finalizing an already-finalized auction, withdrawing from an uninitialized vault).

annotations.common_vuln: Missing state enum check before mutation

properties.remediation: Define an explicit state enum and validate the current state before every mutation with a `require!()` or `match` guard.

properties.name: CPI Cross-Instruction Assumptions
properties.invariant_template: A CPI caller MUST NOT assume the callee's return data or state effects without post-CPI validation.
properties.description: After a CPI call, the calling program assumes success or specific state changes without checking the return data or re-reading the modified accounts, leaving the program vulnerable to a callee that fails silently or returns unexpected data.

annotations.common_vuln: No post-CPI account reload or return data check
annotations.pattern: invoke() followed by immediate state mutation without reload

properties.remediation: After every CPI, reload affected accounts and validate expected post-conditions before continuing.

properties.name: Account Type Cosplay / Discriminator Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every account deserialized as type T MUST carry T's discriminator, so an account of a different type with a compatible layout can never be accepted as T.
properties.description: A program deserializes account data without checking an 8-byte (Anchor) or explicit type tag. An attacker passes an account of another type of the same program (identical field layout, e.g. a User account where an Admin account is expected) and inherits its privileges.

annotations.anchor_constraint: Account<'info, T> (checks owner + discriminator); #[account] / #[derive(InitSpace)] types get a discriminator automatically
annotations.common_vuln: Manual BorshDeserialize::try_from_slice on AccountInfo data, or UncheckedAccount used as a typed account
annotations.formal_invariant: forall ix, forall a in ctx.accounts typed T: a.data[0..8] == DISC(T)  AND  DISC(T) != DISC(U) for all U != T
anchor_checks: Declare every typed account as Account<'info, T> / AccountLoader<'info, T>
If manual deserialization is unavoidable, call T::try_deserialize (checks discriminator) instead of try_from_slice
Give each account struct a distinct discriminator (default Anchor behaviour) or an explicit enum tag

static_rules.rule: Flag any BorshDeserialize::try_from_slice / try_from_slice_unchecked applied to AccountInfo data.
Flag UncheckedAccount/AccountInfo fields whose data is later deserialized into a program-defined struct.
Flag two program account structs with identical field layouts that lack distinct discriminators (non-Anchor programs).

attacker_test.name: type_cosplay_privileged_account
attacker_test.setup: Program has two account types A (user) and B (admin) with identical layout; privileged ix expects B.
attacker_test.attack: Mallory calls the privileged ix passing an A account she controls in the B slot.
attacker_test.expected: Transaction fails with AccountDiscriminatorMismatch (Anchor error 3002) or an explicit tag error; no state change.

static.note: Pattern + account-struct inspection finds manual deserialization and untyped accounts.

dynamic.note: Anchor test passes a same-layout foreign-type account and asserts rejection.

formal.note: Kani can prove a pure deserialize-guard function rejects any buffer whose tag != DISC(T); real account loading is not modelled.

properties.remediation: Use Account<'info, T> or AccountLoader; for manual parsing use T::try_deserialize so the discriminator is verified.

properties.name: Account Re-initialization
properties.invariant_template: An initialization instruction MUST succeed at most once per account; an already-initialized account MUST NOT be re-initialized or have its authority overwritten.
properties.description: An initialize instruction can run on an account that already holds state (init_if_needed without guards, manual create_account/data writes without an is_initialized check). An attacker re-initializes a victim's account and replaces its authority or balances.

annotations.anchor_constraint: #[account(init, payer = ..., space = ...)] (fails if the account already exists); avoid init_if_needed unless guarded
annotations.common_vuln: init_if_needed without checking existing authority; manual initialization without an is_initialized flag
annotations.formal_invariant: forall acct: initialize(acct) is enabled only if state(acct) == Uninitialized; after success state(acct) == Initialized AND authority is unchanged by any later initialize call
anchor_checks: Use #[account(init, ...)] for one-time setup
If init_if_needed is required, add constraint on existing authority and guard the handler with require!(!acct.is_initialized)
Store an is_initialized flag (or a state enum) for non-Anchor initialization paths

static_rules.rule: Flag every use of init_if_needed (requires manual review of the handler guard).
Flag initialize-style handlers (name matches initiali[sz]e|setup|create) that write authority/owner fields without reading an is_initialized flag or state enum first.
Flag system_program::create_account / allocate+assign performed without a preceding data-length or lamports==0 check.

attacker_test.name: reinitialize_overwrites_authority
attacker_test.setup: Alice initializes vault V with authority=Alice and deposits funds.
attacker_test.attack: Mallory calls initialize on V again with authority=Mallory.
attacker_test.expected: Second initialize fails (account already in use / custom AlreadyInitialized); V.authority stays Alice.

static.note: init_if_needed and unguarded initialize handlers are syntactically identifiable.

dynamic.note: Call initialize twice with different authorities and assert second call reverts.

formal.note: State-machine model (Uninitialized -> Initialized) extracted from handler logic is a good Kani target.

properties.remediation: Use plain init, or guard init_if_needed handlers with an explicit initialized flag and authority check.

properties.name: Account Closing / Revival Safety
properties.invariant_template: A closed account MUST have its lamports transferred out, its data zeroed and its discriminator invalidated, so it cannot be revived or reused within the same transaction.
properties.description: An account is 'closed' only by moving lamports, leaving data and discriminator intact. In the same transaction an attacker refunds rent so the account survives the runtime's garbage collection and its stale state is used again (revival attack).

annotations.anchor_constraint: #[account(mut, close = receiver)] (zeroes data and sets the CLOSED_ACCOUNT_DISCRIMINATOR)
annotations.common_vuln: Manual lamport zeroing without clearing data / discriminator; closing without verifying the receiver
annotations.formal_invariant: after close(acct): lamports(acct) == 0 AND data(acct) == zeros OR disc(acct) == CLOSED; and any later ix using acct in the same tx fails discriminator check
anchor_checks: Always close via #[account(close = receiver)] with receiver constrained (has_one / Signer)
If closing manually: zero data, write CLOSED_ACCOUNT_DISCRIMINATOR, then move lamports
Constrain the lamport receiver to the authority, never an arbitrary account

static_rules.rule: Flag manual lamport zeroing (**x.lamports.borrow_mut() = 0) in a handler that does not also write the closed discriminator or zero the data.
Flag close = target where target is not a Signer and has no has_one/address constraint.
Flag AccountInfo::assign(&system_program::ID) / realloc(0) closes without data clearing.

attacker_test.name: close_then_revive_same_tx
attacker_test.setup: Program exposes close_vault (manual lamport transfer) and deposit.
attacker_test.attack: In one transaction: close_vault, then a system transfer refunding rent, then withdraw using the stale vault state.
attacker_test.expected: Third instruction fails (closed/invalid discriminator); stale balance cannot be used.

static.note: Manual-close idioms and unconstrained close receivers are pattern-detectable.

dynamic.note: Needs a multi-instruction transaction on the local validator.

formal.note: Kani can check the close function's postcondition on a modelled account struct; runtime GC is not modelled.

properties.remediation: Close accounts with Anchor's close constraint, or clear data and set the closed discriminator before transferring lamports.

properties.name: SPL Token Account Validation
properties.invariant_template: Every token account used in a transfer/mint/burn MUST be validated for its mint, its owner/authority and the token program that owns it.
properties.description: A program accepts token accounts without checking that the mint matches the expected mint, that the token owner is the expected authority, or that the token program is the real SPL Token program. An attacker substitutes a worthless mint or a token account they control.

annotations.anchor_constraint: #[account(token::mint = mint, token::authority = authority)] / associated_token::*; token_program: Program<'info, Token>
annotations.common_vuln: Token accounts typed as AccountInfo/UncheckedAccount; missing token::mint or token::authority; unchecked token_program
annotations.formal_invariant: forall transfer(src, dst, amt): src.mint == EXPECTED_MINT AND dst.mint == EXPECTED_MINT AND src.owner_auth == signer_or_pda AND token_program.key == spl_token::ID
anchor_checks: Use Account<'info, TokenAccount> / InterfaceAccount<'info, TokenAccount>
Add token::mint and token::authority (or associated_token::mint/authority) constraints
Use Program<'info, Token> (or Token2022 via Interface) for the token program

static_rules.rule: Flag fields named *token*|*mint*|*vault*|*ata* typed AccountInfo/UncheckedAccount.
Flag Account<'info, TokenAccount> fields in a struct used by a transfer handler that have neither token::mint nor an equivalent constraint.
Flag token_program fields not typed Program<'info, Token>.

attacker_test.name: wrong_mint_token_account
attacker_test.setup: Pool expects mint M. Mallory creates mint X and a funded token account of mint X.
attacker_test.attack: Mallory calls deposit/swap passing her mint-X account in the mint-M slot.
attacker_test.expected: Fails with ConstraintTokenMint (Anchor error 2014) or custom error; pool balances unchanged.

static.note: Account types and constraints on token accounts are visible in the Accounts struct.

dynamic.note: Create a second mint on the local validator and attempt substitution.

formal.note: Requires modelling SPL Token program state; Kani cannot execute it. Only the pure comparison logic can be modelled, which adds little.

properties.remediation: Add token::mint / token::authority constraints and use Program<'info, Token> for the token program.

properties.name: Arbitrary CPI / PDA Signer-Seeds Misuse
properties.invariant_template: A CPI MUST only target a program whose ID is fixed or validated, and PDA signer seeds MUST be derived from program-controlled values, never attacker-supplied ones.
properties.description: The CPI target program or the seeds used with invoke_signed come from user input. An attacker redirects the call to a malicious program, or supplies seeds that make the program sign for a PDA it should not control, leading to privilege escalation or fund theft. Complements SOL-05 (program-id check) by covering signer seeds and call arguments.

annotations.anchor_constraint: Program<'info, T>; CpiContext::new_with_signer with seeds built from constants and validated accounts
annotations.common_vuln: invoke/invoke_signed with a user-supplied program AccountInfo; seeds taken from instruction data
annotations.formal_invariant: forall cpi(target, seeds): target.key IN ALLOWED_PROGRAMS AND seeds == CANONICAL_SEEDS(validated_accounts) AND signer PDA == find_program_address(seeds)
anchor_checks: Type the CPI program as Program<'info, T> or add address = EXPECTED_ID
Build signer seeds only from constants and fields of validated accounts
Verify the signing PDA with seeds + bump constraints (see SOL-03) before invoke_signed

static_rules.rule: Flag invoke/invoke_signed whose program argument originates from an AccountInfo/UncheckedAccount field.
Flag CpiContext::new_with_signer / invoke_signed where any seed expression references instruction arguments.
Flag Instruction { program_id: <account>.key() } constructed from an unvalidated account.

attacker_test.name: arbitrary_cpi_fake_program
attacker_test.setup: Program performs a CPI to the token program from instruction 'payout'.
attacker_test.attack: Mallory deploys a fake program with the same interface and passes it as the target program.
attacker_test.expected: Fails with InvalidProgramId / IncorrectProgramId; the fake program is never invoked.

static.note: CPI call sites and the provenance of program/seed expressions are syntactic.

dynamic.note: Deploy a decoy program to the local validator and attempt the redirect.

formal.note: Kani cannot execute invoke/invoke_signed or syscalls. Only an abstract allowlist check on extracted logic can be proven; document as unverified surface.

properties.remediation: Pin CPI targets with Program<'info, T>, and derive signer seeds only from constants and validated accounts.

properties.name: Unvalidated remaining_accounts
properties.invariant_template: Every account read from ctx.remaining_accounts MUST be validated (owner, type, signer/writable flags, expected key or derivation) as strictly as a declared account.
properties.description: Anchor's declared accounts are validated automatically, but remaining_accounts are raw AccountInfos. Handlers that iterate them and read/write data or transfer lamports without checks let an attacker smuggle arbitrary accounts into privileged logic.

annotations.anchor_constraint: None automatic; use manual Account::try_from(&ai) plus key/owner/seeds checks, or declare accounts explicitly
annotations.common_vuln: for ai in ctx.remaining_accounts { ... } with no owner/key/signer validation
annotations.formal_invariant: forall ai in remaining_accounts used by handler: validated(ai) where validated = owner(ai)==EXPECTED_OWNER AND disc(ai)==DISC(T) AND key(ai)==EXPECTED_KEY(ctx) AND (needs_signer => ai.is_signer)
anchor_checks: Prefer declaring accounts in the Accounts struct over remaining_accounts
Convert with Account::<T>::try_from(ai) (owner + discriminator)
Compare ai.key() with an expected or derived address; check is_signer / is_writable as needed
Bound the number of remaining accounts and reject duplicates

static_rules.rule: Flag any use of ctx.remaining_accounts.
Escalate to high when an element is used for lamports/data mutation or as a CPI account without a preceding key/owner check.
Flag loops over remaining_accounts with no duplicate-key check.

attacker_test.name: remaining_accounts_smuggling
attacker_test.setup: Handler 'distribute' pays every account in remaining_accounts a fixed share.
attacker_test.attack: Mallory appends her own account (and a duplicate of a legitimate recipient) to remaining_accounts.
attacker_test.expected: Instruction fails on key/owner/duplicate validation, or Mallory receives nothing.

static.note: remaining_accounts usage is trivially detectable; validation presence is checked by rule.

dynamic.note: Attacker appends crafted accounts; assert rejection / no payout.

formal.note: If the per-account validation loop is extracted into pure logic, Kani can prove no unvalidated element is consumed.

properties.remediation: Declare accounts explicitly, or validate every remaining account's owner, discriminator, key and signer flags before use.

properties.name: Lamport Conservation & Rent-Exemption
properties.invariant_template: Instruction execution MUST conserve total lamports (no creation/destruction by program logic) and every non-closed program-owned account MUST remain rent-exempt.
properties.description: Direct lamport manipulation (borrow_mut_lamports) can mint or burn value, drop accounts below the rent-exempt minimum, or make the instruction fail at runtime sanity checks. Incorrect accounting lets an attacker drain a vault or leave accounts that the runtime later purges.

annotations.anchor_constraint: #[account(mut, rent_exempt = enforce)]; prefer system_program::transfer CPIs over raw lamport edits
annotations.common_vuln: Manual lamport arithmetic; withdraw leaving account below rent minimum; unchecked sub on lamports
annotations.formal_invariant: SUM(lamports_before over touched accounts) == SUM(lamports_after) AND forall acct not closed: lamports_after(acct) >= Rent::minimum_balance(acct.data_len)
anchor_checks: Use system_program::transfer for SOL moves where the source is system-owned; use checked_sub/checked_add for program-owned lamport edits
After mutation assert source lamports >= Rent::get()?.minimum_balance(data_len)
Add rent_exempt = enforce constraint on mutable program accounts

static_rules.rule: Flag direct lamports.borrow_mut() / try_borrow_mut_lamports() edits.
Flag lamport arithmetic using unchecked +/-/ += / -= operators.
Flag handlers that reduce a program-owned account's lamports with no Rent::minimum_balance comparison.

attacker_test.name: withdraw_below_rent_exempt
attacker_test.attack: Mallory (or Alice) withdraws rent-minimum + 1000 (full amount) and in a second case amount causing underflow.
attacker_test.expected: Withdraw capped/rejected so lamports >= rent minimum; sum of lamports before == after; no underflow panic escapes as state corruption.

static.note: Raw lamport edits and unchecked arithmetic are detectable; whether accounting is correct is not.

dynamic.note: Compare balances before/after on the local validator and test rent boundary values.

formal.note: Conservation of a sum over modelled account lamport fields is a strong Kani/bounded-model target.

properties.remediation: Use checked arithmetic, prefer transfer CPIs, and assert rent-exempt minimum after every lamport mutation.

properties.name: Account Realloc / Data-Size Integrity
properties.invariant_template: Any change to an account's data length MUST be authorized, bounded (<= MAX_PERMITTED_DATA_INCREASE per instruction and 10 MiB total), funded for rent, and leave all stored fields consistent with the new length.
properties.description: Unchecked realloc or a mismatch between declared space and the serialized struct size lets an attacker grow accounts to exhaust payer funds, shrink accounts to truncate state, or trigger deserialization of stale/garbage bytes.

annotations.anchor_constraint: #[account(mut, realloc = new_len, realloc::payer = payer, realloc::zero = true)]; #[derive(InitSpace)] for space
annotations.common_vuln: Manual realloc without payer/rent top-up; realloc::zero = false when shrinking then growing; hard-coded space not matching struct
annotations.formal_invariant: forall realloc(acct, n): signer is acct authority AND n <= data_len + 10240 AND n >= MIN_STRUCT_LEN AND lamports(acct) >= rent_min(n) AND bytes beyond old_len are zeroed
anchor_checks: Use realloc constraints with payer and zero = true
Derive space from #[derive(InitSpace)] rather than literals
Restrict who may realloc (has_one = authority)
Bound dynamic Vec/String sizes with explicit max lengths

static_rules.rule: Flag AccountInfo::realloc / resize calls outside an Anchor realloc constraint.
Flag realloc::zero = false.
Flag space = <integer literal> on structs containing Vec/String (space may not fit).

attacker_test.name: realloc_abuse_and_truncation
attacker_test.setup: Account with a list field supports append (realloc grow).
attacker_test.attack: Mallory (non-authority) triggers realloc; separately a call requests growth beyond 10240 bytes and a shrink below the struct minimum.
attacker_test.expected: Non-authority rejected; oversize and undersize requests fail; surviving data deserializes consistently.

static.note: Realloc call sites and constraint flags are syntactic.

dynamic.note: Grow/shrink/boundary cases on the local validator.

formal.note: Size arithmetic and bounds (no overflow, <= limits) are provable on extracted logic; runtime realloc semantics are not modelled.

properties.remediation: Use Anchor realloc constraints with payer and zero=true, derive space via InitSpace, and restrict reallocation to the authority.

default_selection.rationale: SOL-10 has the weakest verification coverage (static: partial, dynamic: partial, formal: no) and stays opt-in until a mock-CPI test harness improves it.
rules: Run static and dynamic checks wherever the property supports them.
Run Kani only for properties whose formal rating is yes or partial.
Report runtime-dependent checks that cannot be verified as unverified_surface; never overclaim verification.
